def: A long-term plan setting out how the organisation will attract, develop, organise and keep the people it needs to deliver its business goals.

formal.ex: The Board approved the three-year [[people strategy]] at its March meeting.

everyday.ex: Our [[HR strategy]] has to follow the business plan, not the other way round.

note_fr: « People strategy » est de plus en plus courant dans les groupes anglo-saxons, surtout là où la DRH s'appelle « Chief People Officer ». « Strategy » se prononce avec l'accent sur la première syllabe : /ˈstræt-/.

fr: aligner la stratégie RH sur la stratégie de l'entreprise

term.uk: to align HR with the business strategy
term.us: to align HR with the business strategy

ipa.uk: /tu əˈlaɪn ˌeɪtʃ ˈɑː wɪð ðə ˈbɪznəs ˈstrætədʒi/
ipa.us: /tu əˈlaɪn ˌeɪtʃ ˈɑːr wɪð ðə ˈbɪznəs ˈstrætədʒi/

def: To make sure that HR priorities, budgets and programmes directly support what the business is trying to achieve.

formal.uk: to ensure alignment with the business strategy
formal.us: to ensure alignment with the business strategy
formal.ex: Each initiative in the roadmap has been reviewed [[to ensure alignment with the business strategy]].

everyday.uk: to align HR with the business
everyday.us: to align HR with the business
everyday.ex: If we don't [[align HR with the business]], we'll keep running programmes nobody asked for.

collocations: to be out of step with
to link HR objectives to business goals
note_fr: On dit « align with » (et non « align on », sauf dans « to align on a decision » = se mettre d'accord). « Alignment » s'écrit sans « e » après le « g ».

def: A plan showing the main HR projects, their order and their timing over a given period, usually one to three years.

formal.ex: The [[HR roadmap]] for 2027 comprises four workstreams, each with a named executive sponsor.

everyday.ex: I'll walk you through the [[roadmap]] and then we can discuss what drops off if the budget is cut.

note_fr: « Roadmap » s'écrit en un seul mot. « Is it on the roadmap? » signifie « est-ce prévu ? » : expression très fréquente dans les réunions.

def: The small number of objectives an organisation has decided to focus its effort and money on.

formal.ex: The proposal is consistent with the Group's [[strategic priorities]] for the coming year.

everyday.ex: Retention and manager capability are our two [[top priorities]] this year.

note_fr: En anglais, trop de priorités n'en sont plus : « if everything is a priority, nothing is ». Évitez « the first priority » ; dites « the top priority » ou « our number-one priority ».

def: To decide which tasks or projects are most important and deal with them first.

formal.ex: Resources will be allocated to [[prioritise]] initiatives with a measurable business impact.
formal.ex_us: Resources will be allocated to [[prioritize]] initiatives with a measurable business impact.

everyday.ex: Given the budget, I'd [[put retention first]] and park the new HRIS until next year.

collocations: to put something on the back burner
note_fr: Orthographe UK « prioritise » / US « prioritize ». « Hiérarchiser » se traduit aussi par « to rank ». « To park something » = mettre de côté pour plus tard.

def: A senior HR professional attached to a business unit who advises its leaders on all people matters.

formal.ex: Each business unit is supported by a dedicated [[HR business partner]] reporting to the HR Director.

everyday.ex: Speak to your [[HRBP]] before you have that conversation.

collocations: to act as a business partner
note_fr: Le sigle se prononce lettre par lettre : « aitch-ar-bee-pee ». En France on garde souvent le terme anglais ; ne le traduisez pas par « partenaire d'affaires RH ».

def: The money allocated to the HR function and to people costs for a given year.

formal.ex: The [[HR budget]] for the coming financial year is presented in Appendix 2.
formal.ex_us: The [[HR budget]] for the coming fiscal year is presented in Appendix 2.

everyday.ex: We're already over [[budget]] on agency fees, so the training spend will have to wait.

note_fr: « Financial year » (UK) / « fiscal year » (US) pour l'exercice. « To be over budget » = dépasser le budget ; « under budget » = rester en deçà.

def: A decision to stop recruiting new staff, except for a few authorised exceptions, usually to control costs.

formal.ex: A [[recruitment freeze]] will apply from 1 October, save for business-critical roles approved by the CFO.
formal.ex_us: A [[hiring freeze]] will apply from October 1, except for business-critical roles approved by the CFO.

everyday.ex: We're under a [[hiring freeze]] until Q2, so any replacement needs a business case.

note_fr: « Freeze » s'emploie aussi pour « pay freeze ». On « impose » ou « lift » un gel. Un gel ne signifie pas un licenciement : rassurez les équipes en le précisant.

def: A regular report, often on one page, showing the main HR indicators and how they are changing.

formal.ex: The monthly [[HR dashboard]] is circulated to the executive team on the fifth working day.

everyday.ex: If it isn't on the [[dashboard]], nobody on the board will look at it.

note_fr: « Tableau de bord » ne se traduit pas par « board » ni « table ». « RAG status » (red/amber/green) est le code couleur classique des tableaux de bord britanniques.

def: Figures used to measure the workforce and the effectiveness of HR, such as turnover, absence or time to hire.

formal.ex: The following [[HR metrics]] will be reported quarterly to the Audit Committee.

everyday.ex: Let's look at [[the numbers]] before we decide anything.

note_fr: « Indicator » existe mais « metric » est plus courant dans les entreprises anglo-saxonnes. « Vanity metrics » = indicateurs flatteurs mais inutiles pour décider.

def: The proportion of planned working time lost through unplanned absence, usually expressed as a percentage.

formal.ex: The [[absence rate]] stood at 5.8% in the third quarter, compared with 4.9% a year earlier.

everyday.ex: [[Absence]] is creeping up in the warehouse, and it's mostly short spells on Mondays.

note_fr: « Absenteeism » existe mais « absence rate » est le terme neutre des tableaux de bord. Le mode de calcul varie selon les pays et les entreprises : précisez toujours ce que vous comptez.

fr: d'une année sur l'autre, en glissement annuel
def: Compared with the same period of the previous year.

formal.ex: Voluntary turnover fell by two points [[year on year]].
formal.ex_us: Voluntary turnover fell by two points [[year over year]].

everyday.ex: Overtime's up fifteen per cent [[on last year]].
everyday.ex_us: Overtime's up fifteen percent [[versus last year]].

collocations: compared with the same period last year
note_fr: Vraie différence UK/US : « year on year » (UK) / « year over year » ou « YoY » (US). « Per cent » en deux mots en anglais britannique, « percent » en américain.

def: To follow and measure how something changes over time.

formal.ex: Absence will be [[monitored]] on a monthly basis by site.

everyday.ex: We [[track]] time to hire for every role, not just the senior ones.

note_fr: « Suivre » ne se traduit pas par « follow » dans ce sens : « to follow the absence rate » est un calque. Dites « track » ou « monitor ».

def: A short section at the start of a report that gives busy decision-makers the key points and recommendations.

formal.ex: The [[executive summary]] sets out the three decisions required of the Committee.

everyday.ex: Can you send me a one-page [[summary]] before the meeting? He won't read the full deck.

note_fr: Une synthèse anglo-saxonne commence par la recommandation, pas par le contexte (« bottom line up front »). « TL;DR » (« too long; didn't read ») est familier, à réserver aux échanges internes.

def: The main points the audience should remember from a presentation or meeting.

formal.ex: The [[key points]] arising from the review are summarised below.
formal.ex_us: The [[key points]] arising from the review are summarized below.

everyday.ex: So, three [[key takeaways]] from this quarter's numbers.

note_fr: « Takeaway » est aussi un plat à emporter au Royaume-Uni (« takeout » aux États-Unis) ; le contexte suffit à lever l'ambiguïté.

def: To receive permission to start or continue with a project.

formal.ex: The project may proceed once we [[obtain approval]] from the Executive Committee.

everyday.ex: We [[got the green light]] for the manager programme yesterday.

informal.ex: Have we [[got the go-ahead]] from Mumbai yet?
informal.ex_us: Have we [[gotten the go-ahead]] from Mumbai yet?

collocations: to give something the green light
note_fr: Participe passé : « got » en anglais britannique, « gotten » en américain (« have we gotten... »). « To get the nod » = obtenir l'accord informel.

fr: présenter en détail, expliquer pas à pas
def: To explain something to someone step by step.

formal.ex: I shall [[take the Committee through]] the main assumptions behind the budget.
formal.ex_us: I will [[take the Committee through]] the main assumptions behind the budget.

everyday.ex: Let me [[walk you through]] the slides and then I'll take questions.

note_fr: Le « l » de « walk » ne se prononce pas : /wɔːk/. Ne confondez pas avec « walk-through » (nom) = démonstration, revue pas à pas.

def: To give someone professional guidance on a particular matter.

formal.ex: HR will [[advise on]] the procedure to be followed in each case.

everyday.ex: Can I [[give you some advice]] before you go into that meeting?

collocations: to advise someone to do something
note_fr: Verbe « advise » (avec s, /z/) mais nom « advice » (avec c, /s/), indénombrable : « a piece of advice », jamais « an advice ». « To advise » ne veut pas dire « aviser » au sens de « remarquer ».

def: A conversation in which a manager has to raise a sensitive or unwelcome subject, such as performance or behaviour.

formal.ex: Managers will receive training on how to conduct a [[difficult conversation]] constructively.

everyday.ex: I know it's a [[tough conversation]], but it's kinder to have it now than in six months.

collocations: to prepare for a tough conversation
note_fr: « Entretien » ne se traduit pas par « interview » ici : « interview » renvoie au recrutement ou aux médias. On dit « to have » (et non « to make ») a conversation.

fr: fixer des attentes claires, clarifier ce qu'on attend
def: To tell someone clearly what is expected of them, by when and to what standard.

formal.ex: Managers are responsible for [[setting clear expectations]] at the start of each assignment.

everyday.uk: to be clear about what you expect
everyday.us: to be clear about what you expect
everyday.ex: You need [[to be clear about what you expect]] from him, and by when.

note_fr: « To manage expectations » = éviter que l'interlocuteur n'attende trop, nuance différente de « set ». « Attentes » ne se traduit jamais par « waitings ».

def: To give part of your work or authority to someone else while remaining responsible for the result.

formal.ex: Managers may [[delegate]] day-to-day approvals but remain accountable for the outcome.

everyday.ex: You can't do it all yourself; [[hand the reporting over]] to Priya.
everyday.ex_us: You can't do it all yourself; [[hand the reporting off]] to Priya.

note_fr: Le verbe se prononce /ˈdelɪɡeɪt/, le nom « a delegate » /ˈdelɪɡət/. En droit français, la « délégation de pouvoirs » a des effets juridiques précis : « delegation of authority » en est l'équivalent le plus proche.

def: To control every detail of other people's work instead of trusting them to do it.

formal.ex: The survey suggests that some managers [[exercise excessive control]] over routine decisions.

everyday.ex: If you [[micromanage]] your senior people, they'll leave.

informal.ex: Nobody does their best work with the boss [[breathing down their neck]].

note_fr: S'écrit en un mot. « Micromanagement » est toujours péjoratif ; pour une implication positive, dites « hands-on ».

def: To start dealing with a problem directly.

formal.ex: The manager is expected to [[address the issue]] promptly and to record the steps taken.

everyday.ex: You need to [[deal with it]] now, before the rest of the team notices.

informal.uk: to nip something in the bud
informal.us: to nip something in the bud
informal.ex: Have a word with her this week and [[nip it in the bud]].

collocations: to sweep something under the carpet
note_fr: Faux ami : « to address » ne veut pas dire « adresser » (un courrier se dit « to send »), mais « traiter, s'attaquer à ». « Under the carpet » (UK) / « under the rug » (US).

def: To include someone in a discussion or email exchange so that they are kept informed.

formal.ex: Please [[keep HR informed]] of any further incidents.

everyday.ex: Thanks for flagging this - I'll [[loop in]] our employment lawyer.

collocations: to keep someone in the loop
to be out of the loop
note_fr: « To copy someone in » (UK) / « to cc someone » : mettre en copie. Conseillez aux managers de « loop in HR early » plutôt que d'attendre la crise.

def: A disagreement or tension between two or more people at work that affects how they work together.

formal.ex: Persistent [[interpersonal conflict]] within a team may constitute a psychosocial risk.

everyday.ex: There's been a [[falling-out]] between the two team leads and it's affecting everyone.

informal.ex: There's real [[bad blood]] between those two.

note_fr: Nom : « conflict » /ˈkɒnflɪkt/ (accent sur la 1re syllabe) ; verbe « to conflict » /kənˈflɪkt/. « To fall out » = se brouiller. En France, un conflit persistant peut relever des risques psychosociaux et de l'obligation de sécurité.

def: To contact someone briefly to see how they are or how their work is going.

formal.ex: Managers of remote staff should [[hold regular update meetings]] with each team member.

everyday.ex: I'll [[check in with you]] on Friday to see how it went.

note_fr: Ne pas confondre avec « to check in » (à l'hôtel, à l'aéroport). « To touch base » est un équivalent un peu cliché, très américain.

def: The level of confidence, motivation and satisfaction within a team.

formal.ex: The reorganisation has had a noticeable impact on staff [[morale]].

everyday.ex: [[Team morale]] is at rock bottom since the restructuring was announced.

note_fr: Faux ami : « morale » (avec e) = le moral ; « moral » = la morale, ou l'adjectif moral. Prononciation différente : /məˈrɑːl/ (UK), /məˈræl/ (US).

def: To behave in the way you expect others to behave.

formal.ex: Members of the Leadership Team are expected to [[lead by example]] in applying the new policy.

everyday.ex: If the directors don't take their holidays, nobody will - they need to [[walk the talk]].
everyday.ex_us: If the directors don't take their vacation, nobody will - they need to [[walk the talk]].

note_fr: « Walk the talk » (ou « walk the walk ») = mettre ses actes en accord avec ses paroles. « Practise » (verbe UK) / « practice » (US).

def: To resist or argue against a request, decision or proposal.

formal.ex: HR [[raised objections]] to the proposed timetable on legal grounds.

everyday.ex: I'm going to [[push back]] on the deadline - we can't consult the works council in a week.

note_fr: « To push back » a aussi le sens de « repousser » (une date). Le nom « pushback » est très fréquent : « we got a lot of pushback from the managers ».

def: The way a manager typically makes decisions, communicates and works with a team.

formal.ex: Participants will reflect on their own [[leadership style]] and its impact on others.

everyday.ex: His [[management style]] works in a crisis, but it's wearing people down.

note_fr: « Management » est indénombrable dans ce sens : « the management » désigne aussi la direction. On parle de « style » au singulier, pas « management styles » pour une seule personne.

def: The shared values, beliefs and habits that shape how people behave in an organisation.

formal.ex: The [[corporate culture]] of the Group places strong emphasis on individual accountability.

everyday.ex: It's a very consensual [[company culture]] - nothing gets decided in one meeting.

informal.uk: the way we do things around here
informal.us: the way we do things around here
informal.ex: In the end, culture is just [[the way we do things around here]].

note_fr: « Corporate » se prononce /ˈkɔːpərət/ (trois syllabes en UK). Évitez « enterprise culture », qui évoque l'esprit d'entreprendre.

def: The principles an organisation says guide its decisions and the behaviour of its people.

formal.ex: Integrity and respect are among the Group's [[core values]].

everyday.ex: The [[company values]] are on every wall, but do managers actually live them?

collocations: to be at odds with our values
note_fr: « Value » au pluriel = valeurs morales ; au singulier, c'est souvent la valeur financière. « Core values » est l'expression standard des documents officiels.

def: A written document setting out the company's rules and approach on a people matter, such as travel, remote work or conduct.

formal.ex: This [[HR policy]] applies to all employees of the French subsidiaries with effect from 1 January.
formal.ex_us: This [[HR policy]] applies to all employees of the French subsidiaries effective January 1.

everyday.ex: What does our [[policy]] say about working from abroad?

note_fr: Faux ami : « policy » = une politique, une règle interne ; « politics » = la politique au sens partisan (ou les jeux de pouvoir : « office politics »). En France, une politique RH ne peut contredire le Code du travail ni les accords collectifs ; le règlement intérieur suit une procédure spécifique.

fr: DRH, directeur ou directrice des ressources humaines
def: The most senior HR person in a company or subsidiary, responsible for the whole HR function.

formal.ex: The [[Human Resources Director]] shall be consulted prior to any change in reporting lines.
formal.ex_us: The [[Vice President, Human Resources]] shall be consulted prior to any change in reporting lines.

everyday.ex: I'm the interim [[HR Director]] for the two French entities.
everyday.ex_us: I'm the interim [[head of HR]] for the two French entities.

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, les titres varient : « VP HR », « CHRO », « Chief People Officer ». « DRH » désigne aussi la direction elle-même : « the HR department » ou « HR ».

def: The layer of managers between senior leadership and frontline staff or team leaders.

formal.ex: The plan requires the active involvement of [[middle management]] across all sites.

everyday.ex: The [[middle managers]] are the ones who'll make or break this change.

collocations: to be squeezed in the middle
note_fr: « Management » sans article désigne collectivement les managers. « Delayering » = réduction des niveaux hiérarchiques, sujet fréquent des plans d'organisation.

def: To avoid saying something directly, usually because it is uncomfortable.

formal.ex: In such conversations, managers should [[be direct]] while remaining respectful.

everyday.ex: Don't spend ten minutes on small talk - [[get to the point]] and then listen.

informal.ex: Don't [[beat around the bush]] - tell him the work isn't good enough.

note_fr: Les Britanniques disent aussi « beat about the bush ». « To sugar-coat » = enrober, édulcorer un message désagréable ; à déconseiller aux managers.

def: A job that has been planned and funded in the approved budget for the year.

formal.ex: Only [[budgeted positions]] may be advertised without further approval.

everyday.ex: Is this role in the [[approved headcount]], or are we asking for a new one?

note_fr: « Backfill » = remplacement d'un départ sur le même poste. « Headcount » est indénombrable : « we have headcount for two more people » = nous avons le budget pour deux postes de plus.

def: Based on the analysis of facts and figures rather than on intuition or habit.

formal.ex: We recommend an [[evidence-based]] approach to setting retention targets.

everyday.ex: The CFO wants HR to be more [[data-driven]] - fewer anecdotes, more numbers.

collocations: to back something up with data
note_fr: « Data » se prononce /ˈdeɪtə/ en UK et souvent /ˈdeɪtə/ ou /ˈdætə/ aux États-Unis ; il s'emploie couramment au singulier (« the data shows »), sauf dans un registre très soutenu.

def: The benefit obtained from spending money on something, compared with its cost.

formal.ex: The expected [[return on investment]] of the programme is set out in Section 4.

everyday.ex: The board will ask about the [[ROI]] of the leadership programme, so have a number ready.

note_fr: Le sigle se lit lettre par lettre : « are-oh-eye ». « Value for money » est plus britannique et plus général (rapport qualité-prix).

def: A document or argument showing why a project or expense is justified, with its costs, benefits and risks.

formal.ex: A [[business case]] must accompany any request for additional headcount.

everyday.ex: Put together a [[business case]] and I'll take it to the CFO.

collocations: to put a business case to
note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « commercial case ». Le « business case » est l'outil standard pour obtenir un budget dans les groupes anglo-saxons : coûts, bénéfices, risques, alternatives.

def: To give reasons why something should be done or supported.

formal.uk: to set out the case for
formal.us: to set out the case for
formal.ex: This paper [[sets out the case for]] harmonising remote-working rules across the French entities.
formal.ex_us: This paper [[sets out the case for]] harmonizing remote-working rules across the French entities.

everyday.ex: I'll [[make the case for]] keeping the retention bonus at Thursday's meeting.

note_fr: On dit « make the case for » (et non « plead for », qui évoque une supplication ou le tribunal). « To champion » = porter, défendre activement un projet.

def: A document prepared for the board of directors to inform it or ask it to take a decision.

formal.ex: The [[board paper]] invites the Board to approve the revised remuneration policy.
formal.ex_us: The [[board memorandum]] asks the Board to approve the revised compensation policy.

everyday.ex: The [[board paper]] needs to be with the company secretary by Friday.
everyday.ex_us: The [[board deck]] needs to be with the corporate secretary by Friday.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, un « board paper » se termine souvent par « The Board is invited to... » (décision demandée). Aux États-Unis, on parle plus volontiers de « board deck » (présentation). « Company secretary » (UK) / « corporate secretary » (US).

def: The most important fact or conclusion in a discussion; also the final profit figure of a business.

formal.ex: [[In conclusion]], the risk of maintaining the current approach outweighs its cost.

everyday.ex: [[The bottom line]] is that we can't do this without consulting the works council.

collocations: at the end of the day
note_fr: Deux sens : la conclusion essentielle, et le résultat net (dernière ligne du compte de résultat). « To have an impact on the bottom line » = peser sur la rentabilité.

def: A detailed examination of one particular subject or problem.

formal.ex: A [[detailed review]] of absence at the Lyon site will be presented in June.

everyday.ex: Can we do a [[deep dive]] on turnover in sales at the next ExCo?

collocations: to do a deep dive into
note_fr: Expression très courante dans les comités de direction anglo-saxons. « To drill down into the data » = descendre dans le détail des chiffres.

def: To discuss a point separately after the meeting rather than in front of everyone.

formal.ex: I suggest we [[discuss this separately]] so as not to delay the remaining items.

everyday.ex: That's a fair point, but can we [[take it offline]]? It only concerns the Lille team.

note_fr: Très utile pour éviter qu'un sujet individuel ou sensible soit débattu en comité. Rien à voir avec l'informatique ici.

fr: glisser un mot discrètement à quelqu'un

term.uk: to have a quiet word with someone

ipa.uk: /tu hæv ə ˌkwaɪət ˈwɜːd wɪð ˈsʌmwʌn/

def: To speak to someone privately and informally, usually about a problem with their work or behaviour.

formal.ex: Before any formal step, the manager should [[hold an informal discussion]] with the employee.

everyday.uk: to have a quiet word with someone
everyday.ex: I'd [[have a quiet word with him]] before it turns into a formal issue.
everyday.ex_us: I'd [[pull him aside]] before it turns into a formal issue.

note_fr: Vraie différence UK/US : « a quiet word » est typiquement britannique ; les Américains disent « to pull someone aside » ou « to have a private conversation ». Rappelez aux managers que l'informel ne dispense pas de garder une trace.

def: To talk openly about a disagreement in order to remove tension.

formal.ex: A facilitated meeting may help [[resolve tensions]] between the two departments.

everyday.ex: Get them in a room together and [[clear the air]] - it's been simmering for weeks.

note_fr: « To come to a head » = atteindre un point critique. « To bury the hatchet » = se réconcilier.

def: A situation in which two people do not get on because their characters are very different.

formal.ex: The investigation found no misconduct, only a [[personality clash]] between the two managers.

everyday.ex: They just [[don't get on]], and the team is caught in the middle.
everyday.ex_us: They just [[don't get along]], and the team is caught in the middle.

collocations: to rub someone up the wrong way
note_fr: « To get on » (UK) / « to get along » (US) = bien s'entendre. « To rub someone up the wrong way » (UK) / « the wrong way » (US) = prendre quelqu'un à rebrousse-poil.

def: To lead people who work mainly from home or from different locations.

formal.ex: The module covers the specific challenges of [[managing a distributed team]].

everyday.ex: [[Managing a remote team]] means you have to be much more deliberate about communication.

collocations: out of sight, out of mind
note_fr: « Remote » et non « distant » (qui signifie « froid, distant » pour une personne). « Proximity bias » = tendance à favoriser les salariés présents au bureau.

fr: accompagner une équipe dans le changement

term.uk: to lead a team through change
term.us: to lead a team through change

def: To guide a team through a period of transformation, explaining it and supporting people as they adapt.

formal.ex: Managers have a central role in [[supporting employees through change]].

everyday.uk: to lead a team through change
everyday.us: to lead a team through change
everyday.ex: Your job now is to [[lead the team through the change]], even if you didn't choose it.

note_fr: « Accompagner » ne se traduit pas par « accompany » (qui signifie aller avec quelqu'un physiquement). Dites « support », « guide » ou « lead through ».

fr: manager son manager, gérer sa hiérarchie
def: To build a good working relationship with your boss so as to influence decisions and get what you need.

formal.ex: Effective HR leaders know how to [[manage upwards]] as well as across the organisation.
formal.ex_us: Effective HR leaders know how to [[manage up]] as well as across the organization.

everyday.ex: You need to [[manage upwards]] a bit more - he doesn't know half of what you do.
everyday.ex_us: You need to [[manage up]] a bit more - he doesn't know half of what you do.

note_fr: Différence UK/US : « upwards » (UK) / « up » (US). « No surprises » est la règle d'or : ne laissez jamais votre supérieur découvrir un problème par quelqu'un d'autre.

fr: obtenir l'adhésion de quelqu'un, embarquer quelqu'un
def: To persuade someone to support a project or idea.

formal.ex: We will need to [[secure the support of]] the regional directors before launch.

everyday.ex: If we can [[bring the plant manager on board]], the others will follow.

note_fr: « On board » s'emploie aussi pour un nouvel arrivant (« welcome on board »). « Embarquer quelqu'un » en ce sens se dit « bring on board » ou « win over ».

def: To question whether something is right, true or the best option.

formal.ex: The Committee [[questioned]] the assumptions underlying the attrition forecast.

everyday.ex: Part of my job is to [[challenge]] the business when a decision carries legal risk.

note_fr: Faux ami partiel : « challenger » en français (mettre au défi, pousser) se dit plutôt « to stretch » ou « to push » ; « to challenge » veut d'abord dire contester. « A challenge » = une difficulté, un défi.

def: To argue against an idea, even if you agree with it, to test how strong it is.

formal.ex: Allow me to [[test the argument]] by considering the opposite view.

everyday.ex: Let me [[play devil's advocate]] for a moment: what if the works council says no?

note_fr: Formule utile pour contredire un dirigeant sans s'opposer personnellement. « Advocate » se prononce /ˈædvəkət/ (nom), le verbe « to advocate » /ˈædvəkeɪt/.

def: A professional whose advice senior leaders seek and rely on.

formal.ex: The HR Director acts as a [[trusted adviser]] to the CEO on all people matters.
formal.ex_us: The HR Director acts as a [[trusted advisor]] to the CEO on all people matters.

everyday.ex: She's become the CEO's [[go-to person]] on anything sensitive.

collocations: to act as a sounding board
note_fr: Orthographe : « adviser » plus fréquent en UK, « advisor » en US (les deux existent). « Sounding board » = interlocuteur avec qui l'on teste ses idées.

fr: avoir voix au chapitre, siéger là où se prennent les décisions
def: A position that allows you to take part in important decisions.

formal.ex: HR must have [[a role in decision-making]] from the earliest stage of any transformation.

everyday.ex: If HR wants [[a seat at the table]], we have to talk the language of the business.

collocations: to earn a seat at the table
note_fr: Expression emblématique du débat sur le rôle stratégique des RH. « To have a say » = avoir son mot à dire.

fr: sauf votre respect, avec tout le respect que je vous dois
def: A polite phrase used before disagreeing with someone, often someone senior.

formal.ex: [[With respect]], I do not believe the proposal reflects the legal position in France.

everyday.ex: [[I take your point, but]] the timing simply doesn't work under French law.
everyday.ex_us: [[I hear you, but]] the timing simply doesn't work under French law.

collocations: I see where you're coming from
note_fr: Attention : « with all due respect » annonce souvent un désaccord net et peut sonner agressif, surtout en anglais britannique. Préférez « I take your point, but... » (UK) ou « I hear you, but... » (US).

def: To understand the mood and attitudes of people in a meeting and adjust what you say.

formal.ex: It is advisable to [[gauge the mood]] of the Committee before presenting the proposal.

everyday.ex: He didn't [[read the room]] - joking about job cuts the day after the announcement.

note_fr: « Gauge » se prononce /ɡeɪdʒ/. « Tone-deaf » = maladroit, insensible au contexte (au sens figuré).

def: To use your higher authority to reject someone else's decision or opinion.

formal.ex: The CEO may [[overrule]] the recommendation, in which case the decision will be recorded.

everyday.ex: If the VP [[overrules]] us, I want it in writing that we advised against it.

informal.ex: He couldn't win the argument, so he [[pulled rank]].

note_fr: « To overrule » vise une personne ou une décision ; « to override » une règle, un système ou une priorité. « To pull rank » = faire valoir sa position hiérarchique.

def: To become involved in a situation, especially to help solve a problem.

formal.ex: HR will [[intervene]] where the informal approach has not resolved the matter.

everyday.ex: At what point should I [[step in]]? They're adults, after all.

note_fr: « Step in » = intervenir ; « step up » = prendre davantage de responsabilités ; « step down » = démissionner d'une fonction ; « step back » = prendre du recul.

def: A style of management based on giving orders and checking that they are obeyed, with little consultation.

formal.ex: [[Directive leadership]] may be appropriate in a crisis but is rarely sustainable.

everyday.ex: It's very [[command-and-control]] over there - nobody makes a decision without the boss.

note_fr: Les tirets s'emploient quand l'expression est adjectivale (« a command-and-control style »). « Autoritaire » ne se traduit pas par « authoritative », qui signifie « qui fait autorité, fiable » ; dites « authoritarian » ou « directive ».

def: Personally involved in the day-to-day work rather than only directing it.

formal.ex: The Director has been [[closely involved]] in the operational aspects of the project.

everyday.ex: She's a very [[hands-on]] manager - sometimes too much.

note_fr: « Hands-off » = en retrait, qui laisse faire. « To be in the weeds » (US) = être noyé dans les détails.

def: Friendly and easy to talk to, so that people feel comfortable raising issues.

formal.ex: Managers should remain [[accessible]] to their teams, particularly during the transition.

everyday.ex: He's clever, but he isn't [[approachable]], so problems reach him too late.

note_fr: « Accessible » existe mais renvoie souvent aux locaux ou au handicap ; pour une personne, « approachable » est plus naturel. « Open-door policy » = porte toujours ouverte.

def: The group of top managers who run a company or a business unit.

formal.ex: The proposal was endorsed by the [[senior leadership team]] on 12 May.
formal.ex_us: The proposal was endorsed by the [[senior leadership team]] on May 12.

everyday.ex: It's on the agenda for [[SLT]] next week.
everyday.ex_us: It's on the agenda for the [[leadership team]] next week.

note_fr: « SLT » est très courant au Royaume-Uni ; aux États-Unis on dit plutôt « the leadership team » ou « the C-suite » (les dirigeants dont le titre commence par « Chief »).

def: The ability to understand and manage your own emotions and to recognise those of others.

formal.ex: [[Emotional intelligence]] is one of the six behaviours assessed in the leadership framework.

everyday.ex: Technically brilliant, but his [[EQ]] is close to zero.

note_fr: « EQ » (/ˌiː ˈkjuː/) est l'abréviation courante, par analogie avec « IQ ». « Sensible » est un faux ami : « sensitive » = sensible, « sensible » = raisonnable.

def: To show the company's values clearly through your own behaviour.

formal.ex: Senior managers are expected to [[embody the values]] of the Group in all their dealings.

everyday.ex: It's not about posters - leaders have to [[live the values]] every day.

note_fr: « Embody » /ɪmˈbɒdi/ est soutenu ; « live the values » est l'équivalent oral. « To uphold » = défendre, faire respecter.

def: An organisation that people actively want to work for because of its reputation and conditions.

formal.ex: Our ambition is to become an [[employer of choice]] in the logistics sector.

everyday.ex: We can't claim to be [[a great place to work]] if managers ignore the survey.

note_fr: « Attractif » se dit « attractive » pour un salaire ou une offre, mais pour un employeur on préfère « an employer of choice ». Ne dites pas « an attractive employer ».

def: To make sure that a rule or policy is actually followed and that breaches have consequences.

formal.ex: Line managers are responsible for [[enforcing the policy]] consistently within their teams.

everyday.ex: If you don't [[apply the rules consistently]], you'll have no leg to stand on later.

note_fr: « Enforce » ne veut pas dire « renforcer » (« to reinforce »). En France, une application incohérente d'une règle interne affaiblit toute sanction ultérieure ; d'où l'importance de « consistency ».

def: To test a new scheme on a small scale before introducing it more widely.

formal.ex: The scheme will be [[piloted]] at two sites before any decision on wider deployment.

everyday.ex: Let's [[trial]] it in one team first and see what breaks.
everyday.ex_us: Let's [[test]] it in one team first and see what breaks.

note_fr: Faux ami : « piloter un projet » se dit « to run / lead / steer a project » ; « to pilot » signifie tester à petite échelle. « To trial » (verbe) est surtout britannique.

def: To lead a project or change actively and push it forward.

formal.ex: The HR Director will [[lead]] the programme, supported by a cross-functional steering group.

everyday.ex: Who's going to [[drive]] this? It can't just sit with HR.

collocations: to be in the driving seat
note_fr: « Driving seat » (UK) / « driver's seat » (US) = aux commandes. « To drive results » est un peu jargonnant mais omniprésent dans les groupes américains.

def: Managers who directly supervise operational employees, such as team leaders and supervisors.

formal.ex: Training will be provided to all [[first-line managers]] before the policy takes effect.

everyday.ex: Our [[frontline managers]] were promoted for being good technicians, not good managers.

note_fr: « Manager de proximité » n'a pas d'équivalent littéral : « proximity manager » n'existe pas. « Frontline » s'écrit en un mot ou avec un tiret (« front-line »).

def: To accept full responsibility for a task or problem and its outcome.

formal.ex: Each director will [[assume responsibility]] for the action plan in their area.

everyday.ex: I need the managers to [[take ownership]] of the survey results, not hand them back to HR.

note_fr: « To own » (« who owns this? ») = qui est responsable ? Très fréquent dans les entreprises américaines. « To pass the buck » = se renvoyer la balle.

def: An immediate response made without thinking it through.

formal.ex: A [[hasty decision]] at this stage would expose the company to significant risk.

everyday.ex: Firing him on the spot would be a [[knee-jerk reaction]] - and a costly one.

collocations: to act in the heat of the moment
note_fr: « To sleep on it » = laisser passer la nuit avant de décider : conseil précieux face à un manager en colère.

def: A series of documents that shows what has happened and when.

formal.ex: Managers must keep a [[written record]] of each informal discussion.

everyday.ex: Without a [[paper trail]], it's his word against yours.

note_fr: Même si les échanges sont électroniques, on dit toujours « paper trail ». Un simple e-mail récapitulatif (« follow-up email ») après un entretien informel suffit souvent à en créer une.

def: To establish the mood or standard of behaviour for what follows.

formal.ex: The CEO's opening remarks will [[set the tone]] for the consultation process.

everyday.ex: The way you handle the first complaint will [[set the tone]] for the whole team.

note_fr: « To send the wrong message » = envoyer un mauvais signal. Ne dites pas « give the tone ».

def: A small team of HR specialists, such as reward, talent or employee relations, that designs policies and advises the rest of HR.

formal.ex: Reward and employee relations will be organised as [[centres of expertise]] serving all business units.
formal.ex_us: Reward and employee relations will be organized as [[centers of excellence]] serving all business units.

everyday.ex: That's a question for the reward [[CoE]], not your HRBP.

note_fr: Différence UK/US : « centre of expertise » (UK) / « center of excellence » (US), même sigle « CoE ». Orthographe « centre » / « center ».

fr: modèle opérationnel RH, organisation de la fonction RH
def: The way the HR function is organised to deliver its services: roles, structures, processes and technology.

formal.ex: The proposed [[HR operating model]] clarifies the respective roles of business partners and shared services.

everyday.uk: the way HR is set up
everyday.us: the way HR is set up
everyday.ex: The problem isn't the people, it's [[the way HR is set up]] - everything comes to the HRBPs.

note_fr: « Operating model » désigne l'organisation globale d'une fonction, pas un « modèle » théorique. « Self-service » = libre-service (portails RH pour salariés et managers).

def: An HR organisation built around business partners, centres of expertise and shared services.

formal.ex: The Group adopted a [[three-pillar model]], separating strategic advice from transactional activity.

everyday.ex: We're still on the old [[three-legged stool]], and the HRBPs end up doing admin.

note_fr: Modèle souvent attribué à Dave Ulrich. « Three-legged stool » (tabouret à trois pieds) est l'image familière employée aux États-Unis comme au Royaume-Uni.

def: Total employment costs expressed as a percentage of revenue.

formal.uk: ratio of staff costs to revenue
formal.us: ratio of personnel costs to revenue
formal.ex: The [[ratio of staff costs to revenue]] has risen to 41%, above the Group target.
formal.ex_us: The [[ratio of personnel costs to revenue]] has risen to 41%, above the Group target.

everyday.ex: Head office keeps asking why our [[payroll ratio]] is higher than in the UK.

note_fr: En France, les cotisations patronales pèsent lourd dans la masse salariale : précisez si le ratio est calculé sur le brut ou sur le coût chargé (« fully loaded cost »). « Turnover » est un faux ami ici : en anglais britannique, il signifie aussi chiffre d'affaires.

def: Voluntary departures of employees the company would have preferred to keep, such as high performers.

formal.ex: [[Regretted attrition]] among engineers reached 9% over the last twelve months.

everyday.ex: We're not just losing people, we're [[losing good people]] - and to the same competitor.

note_fr: « Attrition » désigne les départs non remplacés ou l'ensemble des départs selon les entreprises : vérifiez la définition. « To stem » = endiguer.

fr: indicateurs avancés et indicateurs de résultat
def: Leading indicators signal what is likely to happen; lagging indicators measure what has already happened.

formal.ex: The dashboard combines [[leading and lagging indicators]] to give early warning of retention risk.

everyday.ex: Engagement scores are our [[early warning signs]]; turnover only tells us what's already gone wrong.

note_fr: Exemple type : l'engagement ou l'absence de courte durée sont des « leading indicators » ; le turnover est un « lagging indicator ». « Lag » = retard.

def: The use of statistical analysis of workforce data to understand trends and support HR decisions.

formal.ex: The Group intends to invest in [[workforce analytics]], subject to data protection requirements.

everyday.ex: Our [[people analytics]] team found that turnover tracks almost exactly with manager changes.

note_fr: « Analytics » est un nom pluriel en forme mais généralement singulier en sens. En France et dans l'UE, toute analyse de données salariés doit respecter le RGPD et, le cas échéant, la consultation du CSE.

fr: mettre à l'ordre du jour (UK) / reporter (US)
def: In British English, to present a proposal for discussion; in American English, to postpone discussing it.

formal.ex: The HR Director will [[table a proposal]] on hybrid working at the next meeting.
formal.ex_us: The HR Director will [[put forward a proposal]] on hybrid working at the next meeting.

everyday.uk: to put something on the agenda
everyday.us: to put something on the agenda
everyday.ex: Can we [[put the bonus scheme on the agenda]] for March?

note_fr: Piège majeur UK/US : « to table » = soumettre à la discussion au Royaume-Uni, mais ajourner, mettre de côté aux États-Unis. Avec un public mixte, dites « put forward » ou « postpone ».

def: To persuade people to act when you are not their manager and cannot give them orders.

formal.ex: HR business partners must be able to [[influence without authority]] across the matrix.

everyday.uk: to get people to do things without being their boss
everyday.us: to get people to do things without being their boss
everyday.ex: Half of HR is [[getting people to do things without being their boss]].

note_fr: « Influence » se prononce avec l'accent sur la première syllabe : /ˈɪnfluəns/. « To win hearts and minds » = convaincre et rallier.

fr: dire la vérité aux puissants, oser contredire la direction
def: To tell people in authority things they may not want to hear.

formal.ex: The role requires the ability to [[give candid advice]] to the executive team.

everyday.ex: Sometimes HR has to [[speak truth to power]], even if it costs us politically.

collocations: to tell it like it is
note_fr: « Candid » = franc, sincère (faux ami avec « candide », qui se dit « naive »).

def: To have someone important listen to and take account of your views.

formal.ex: The Head of Reward [[has the ear of]] the Remuneration Committee.

everyday.ex: She [[has the CEO's ear]], so it's worth getting her on side first.

note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec « to bend someone's ear » = rebattre les oreilles à quelqu'un. « To get someone on side » (UK) = rallier quelqu'un.

def: A leadership approach in which the leader's main role is to support and develop the team.

formal.ex: The programme draws on the principles of [[servant leadership]].

everyday.ex: His idea of leadership is [[putting the team first]] and clearing obstacles out of their way.

note_fr: « Servant » n'a rien de péjoratif ici. Concept américain, à manier avec nuance dans une culture française plus hiérarchique.

fr: périmètre managérial, étendue des responsabilités d'encadrement
def: The number of people who report directly to one manager.

formal.ex: The target [[span of control]] is eight to ten direct reports per manager.

everyday.ex: With fourteen people, his [[number of direct reports]] is just too high.

collocations: a narrow / wide span of control
note_fr: « Spans and layers » est un classique des projets d'organisation. Ne confondez pas avec le périmètre géographique ou fonctionnel (« scope »).

def: A team climate in which people feel able to speak up, admit mistakes and disagree without fear of humiliation or punishment.

formal.ex: Teams with high [[psychological safety]] report errors earlier and learn faster.

everyday.ex: It's about people [[feeling safe to speak up]] - including telling you you're wrong.

note_fr: Le « p » de « psychological » est muet : /saɪ-/. Ne pas confondre avec la santé mentale (« mental health ») ni avec les risques psychosociaux, notion juridique française.

def: The example and attitude set by senior leaders, which strongly influences behaviour throughout the organisation.

formal.ex: A clear [[tone from the top]] is essential to the credibility of the code of conduct.
formal.ex_us: A clear [[tone at the top]] is essential to the credibility of the code of conduct.

everyday.ex: If the ExCo doesn't [[lead from the top]] on this, managers won't bother.

note_fr: Différence d'usage : « tone from the top » plutôt britannique, « tone at the top » plutôt américain (vocabulaire de la conformité et de l'audit).

def: The overall package of pay, benefits, culture and opportunities that a company offers employees in return for their work.

formal.ex: The [[employee value proposition]] will be refreshed to reflect the new hybrid working model.

everyday.ex: What's our [[EVP]] for engineers if we can't match Paris salaries?

note_fr: Attention : aux États-Unis, « EVP » signifie aussi « Executive Vice President ». Précisez à la première occurrence.

fr: adapté à l'usage, en adéquation avec les besoins
def: Good enough to do the job it was designed for.

formal.ex: The current HRIS is no longer [[fit for purpose]] for a multi-entity organisation.
formal.ex_us: The current HRIS is no longer [[fit for purpose]] for a multi-entity organization.

everyday.ex: The old policy just isn't [[up to the job]] any more.
everyday.ex_us: The old policy just isn't [[up to the job]] anymore.

note_fr: Expression très britannique, comprise aux États-Unis. « Any more » (UK) / « anymore » (US).

def: To make someone answer for their results or behaviour and accept the consequences.

formal.ex: Managers will be [[held accountable]] for the completion of mandatory training in their teams.

everyday.ex: Nobody ever [[made him answer for]] the missed deadlines, so he stopped caring.

note_fr: « Responsible » = qui exécute ; « accountable » = qui doit rendre des comptes in fine (cf. matrice RACI). « Responsabiliser » (au sens de donner de l'autonomie) se dit aussi « to empower ».

def: Identifying the people affected by a project and analysing their influence and attitude towards it.

formal.ex: A [[stakeholder mapping]] exercise identified the plant directors as critical to adoption.

everyday.ex: Before the launch, spend an hour [[working out who matters]] and where they stand.
everyday.ex_us: Before the launch, spend an hour [[figuring out who matters]] and where they stand.

note_fr: « To work out » (UK) / « to figure out » (US) = déterminer. « Blockers » = opposants susceptibles de bloquer ; « champions » = relais favorables.

def: In France, an employee with managerial or professional status under the collective agreement, with specific rules on pension, working time and benefits.

formal.ex: The post is classified as that of an [[employee with cadre status]] under the applicable collective agreement.

everyday.ex: He's a [[cadre]], so he's on a days-based arrangement rather than hours.

note_fr: « Cadre » ne se traduit pas par « executive » (dirigeant) ni par « manager » : beaucoup de cadres n'encadrent personne. L'américain « exempt employee » (exclu du paiement des heures supplémentaires) est un rapprochement imparfait.

explain.written: In France, 'cadre' is a status defined by collective agreements for managerial and professional staff, which carries specific rules on pension schemes, working time arrangements and certain benefits.
explain.spoken: Cadre is a French status for managers and professionals - it's not the same as being a manager, and it comes with its own rules on hours and pensions.

def: A secondary, functional reporting line, alongside the direct (solid-line) hierarchical manager.

formal.ex: The HR Director France has a [[functional reporting line]] to the Group CHRO.

everyday.ex: I report to the country MD, with a [[dotted line]] to the VP HR in Chicago.

collocations: to have a dotted line to
note_fr: « Solid line » = rattachement hiérarchique (qui a le pouvoir de direction et disciplinaire en droit français) ; « dotted line » = rattachement fonctionnel. Utile pour expliquer à un groupe étranger qui est l'employeur juridique.

def: A structure in which employees report to more than one manager, for example a country manager and a global function head.

formal.ex: In a [[matrix organisation]], decision rights must be clearly defined to avoid conflicting instructions.
formal.ex_us: In a [[matrix organization]], decision rights must be clearly defined to avoid conflicting instructions.

everyday.ex: In this [[matrix]], nobody knows who actually signs off on a hire.

note_fr: Orthographe UK « organisation » / US « organization ». En droit français, le lien de subordination n'existe qu'avec l'employeur juridique, quelle que soit la matrice.

term.uk: to expose the company to a claim
term.us: to expose the company to a claim

ipa.uk: /tu ɪkˈspəʊz ðə ˈkʌmpəni tu ə ˈkleɪm/
ipa.us: /tu ɪkˈspoʊz ðə ˈkʌmpəni tu ə ˈkleɪm/

def: To create a risk that an employee or authority will take legal action against the company.

formal.uk: to expose the company to a claim
formal.us: to expose the company to a claim
formal.ex: Proceeding without consultation would [[expose the company to a claim]] for obstruction.

everyday.uk: to leave us open to a claim
everyday.us: to leave us open to a lawsuit
everyday.ex: If you do it that way, it'll [[leave us open to a claim]].
everyday.ex_us: If you do it that way, it'll [[leave us open to a lawsuit]].

note_fr: « Lawsuit » est plus courant aux États-Unis, « claim » au Royaume-Uni (« tribunal claim »). « Exposure » = niveau de risque financier ou juridique.

def: In a French company, the CODIR: the operational management team of a company or site, usually below the executive committee in large groups.

formal.ex: The matter was discussed at the [[management committee]] meeting of 3 March.
formal.ex_us: The matter was discussed at the [[management committee]] meeting of March 3.

everyday.ex: I'll raise it at the [[leadership team]] meeting on Monday.

collocations: to sit on the management committee
note_fr: En France, la distinction COMEX (instance stratégique) / CODIR (pilotage opérationnel) n'a pas d'équivalent exact ; expliquez la composition plutôt que de traduire le sigle.

explain.written: The CODIR (comité de direction) is the management committee that runs a French company or site day to day, generally distinct from the COMEX, which sets group strategy.
explain.spoken: The CODIR is basically the local leadership team - the people who run the business here week to week.

def: To support or form the basis of an argument, strategy or system.

formal.ex: Three principles [[underpin]] the proposed HR strategy: simplicity, fairness and accountability.

everyday.ex: Let me explain the thinking that [[is behind]] the roadmap.

note_fr: Verbe soutenu très utile à l'écrit stratégique. « Rationale » /ˌræʃəˈnɑːl/ = la logique, la justification.
